summary: Replace x by [δ]; the module of a rational determinant is a norm, a product over the infinite places; compare place by place by Cauchy–Schwarz for determinants.

steps.claim: δ is a unit (det(aᴴQb) ≠ 0 and v, v' invertible), so x ≤ [δ] = [det v]·[det(aᴴQb)]·[det v']; for the rational number det(aᴴQb) the module is |N(det aᴴQb)| = ∏_w |Φ_w(det aᴴQb)|² (abs_norm_eq_prod_norm_sq), and likewise for aᴴQa and bᴴQb; both sides become products over the infinite places w.
steps.lean:
grw [i] <;> simp [*, ← RingHom.mapMatrix_apply, ← RingHom.map_det,
    abs_norm_eq_prod_norm_sq, mul_pow, ← Finset.prod_pow, ← Finset.prod_mul_distrib]

steps.claim: Compare factor by factor: it remains to show |Φ_w(det aᴴQb)|² ≤ |Φ_w(det aᴴQa)|·|Φ_w(det bᴴQb)| at every w.

This is Cauchy–Schwarz for determinants (norm_det_sq_le_of_posSemidef) applied to the positive semidefinite block matrix (a | b)ᴴ Φ_w(Q) (a | b) = [[aᴴQa, aᴴQb], [bᴴQa, bᴴQb]] (mapped by Φ_w, which commutes with ᴴ).
steps.lean:
simpa [map_conjTranspose, RingHom.map_det, ← mul_pow, sq_le_sq] using
    norm_det_sq_le_of_posSemidef ((fromBlocks_toBlocks
    _).substr ((hQ _).posSemidef.conjTranspose_mul_mul_same ((a.fromCols b).map _)))
